assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level are a clear, original and lasting advance in precision atomic physics. Katori's magic-wavelength lattice idea removes Doppler and recoil shifts, and the resulting stability opens redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. Few candidates connect so directly to atomic structure and its control.
assessment.attribution: The two credited names are a clean two-person configuration. Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove it to record accuracy and stability with strontium and the frequency-comb link. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, NIST ion-clock teams) contributed to the field, but the supplied credit supports a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories worldwide, with clock comparisons and international redefinition roadmaps in progress. Recognition is timely and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Interplay with the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion trapping prize may be weighed by the committee.
I have not independently verified specific accuracy figures or priority details beyond my existing knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry is a foundational matter-wave technique, now used for measurements of gravity, the fine-structure constant and tests of equivalence and relativity. The concept is original and the sensing applications are growing. It is a natural extension of laser cooling recognition, though impact is uneven across subfields.
assessment.attribution: Four names are credited but only three can be proposed. Pritchard (first atom interferometers, light-pulse beam splitters with Chu-era contributors), Kasevich (atomic-fountain precision and gravimetry) and Bordé (theoretical formulation of light-pulse interferometers) are the most defensible trio. Schmiedmayer's contributions on-chip and with Bose-Einstein condensates are real but more specialised. Steven Chu is not credited and cannot be proposed, which is a gap in the narrative since Chu already holds a prize.
assessment.maturity: Gravimeters and gradiometers are demonstrated and commercialised; large-baseline tests are ongoing. Core demonstrations are well confirmed, while the most ambitious fundamental-physics applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation among four credited people is contested and the prize cap of three forces exclusion.
Relation to earlier prizes in laser cooling complicates the novelty argument.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and rests on the conception and construction of ATLAS and CMS, among the most ambitious instruments in science. The theory was recognised in 2013; recognising the experimental achievement would fill a conspicuous gap.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are widely recognised as founding spokespersons and architects of the experiments, which gives a three-person configuration. The collaborations are enormous, and recognising a few leaders over detector builders, analysts and accelerator physicists is intrinsically contentious.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is fully confirmed and its properties measured over a decade, so the discovery is mature. The timing is well past the 2012 announcement.
uncertainties: Whether institutional-leadership roles equal scientific decisive contribution is a judgement the statutes make difficult.
Large-collaboration attribution is a standing unresolved issue; I cannot independently verify individual roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, with the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes, allows controlled study of Hubbard-type many-body physics. It is conceptually original and now a major tool across condensed matter and atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Five names are credited. The theory proposal (Jaksch, Zoller, Cirac) and the experimental realisation (Greiner, Bloch, Esslinger) are distinct contributions. I propose the experimental trio because the strongest experimental milestones (Mott transition, microscopes, fermionic Hubbard) are with them. Zoller and Cirac are conspicuous theoretical candidates and the choice is an allocation judgement.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed in many laboratories, with maturing fermionic and microscope results. Quantitative advantage over classical methods on hard problems is still being established.
uncertainties: Theory versus experiment allocation is unresolved.
Overlap with the 2001 and 2012 AMO prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect, with experimental observation in HgTe, created a large field of topological matter. It is original, clear and has lasting conceptual influence.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal; Molenkamp led the experimental confirmation in HgTe wells following Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's prediction. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not credited here, so the supplied credit leaves out a significant theory contribution. Hasan's work on 3D materials is also relevant but credited separately and the three selected form a defensible set.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed by multiple independent experiments, including 3D topological insulators. Timing is appropriate, and the 2016 prize covered related topological phase concepts.
uncertainties: Missing credited theory names (not selectable) make fair allocation uncertain.
The overlap with the other topological insulator candidate B031 and the 2016 prize leaves priority questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Creating strongly interacting Fermi gases and the BEC-BCS crossover gave a tunable testbed for pairing physics relevant to superconductors and neutron matter. The cold-atom realisation relies on Feshbach resonances and clean interpretation through universal thermodynamics and vortices.
assessment.attribution: Grimm, Salomon and Thomas are central experimental leaders (molecular BEC, pairing, universal thermodynamics). Ketterle, Jin and Zwierlein also made decisive contributions (vortices, condensation of pairs) and are not credited in the list, which limits the fairness of the configuration. Jin is deceased, which constrains inclusion.
assessment.maturity: Experiments are well confirmed and quantitatively consistent with theory. Impact is mature, although later cold-atom prizes make novelty less sharp.
uncertainties: Credit omitting Ketterle, Zwierlein and Jin makes allocation uncertain.
Relative significance versus other cold-atom candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire flat-band physics with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable system. The theory by Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands and the experiment by Jarillo-Herrero's group revealed the phases, a striking theory-experiment pairing.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio matches a natural prize split between theoretical prediction and experimental discovery. Cao and Fatemi, co-first authors and students of the experiment, are not credited, and the Nobel statutes would rule them out for now, though this should be noted.
assessment.maturity: Rapid and extensive replication; however, the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, so interpretation is not yet fully stable. Recognition is a little early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is not settled.
Credit allocation excludes junior experimenters and sample-sensitive reproducibility issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays use optical tweezers and strong Rydberg interactions to realise quantum simulation and gate operations at scale. The technique is original, with rapid growth, and offers a platform for quantum many-body physics that falls near my own atomic expertise in Rydberg and highly excited states.
assessment.attribution: Five credited names. Lukin's group performed the large programmable simulations, Browaeys and Grangier demonstrated tweezer arrays and blockade, and Saffman proposed and demonstrated gate schemes. Zoller's theory proposals are important too. Selecting three requires excluding other significant contributors, so attribution is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Still maturing; error-corrected operations and quantum advantage are not yet established, and the field is evolving quickly. Recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Premature relative to the other candidates.
Five-way credit with theory-experiment split and no obvious natural three-person configuration.
